bug_semantics: CVE-2025-45855/GHSA-5gr5-vmmr-82g6 claim an unauthenticated arbitrary-file upload RCE at /upload/GoodsCategory/image in erupt <= 1.12.19, allowing a crafted webshell to take over the site. That path is EruptFileController.upload under /erupt-api/file, parameterized as eruptName=GoodsCategory and fieldName=image. GoodsCategory is not in xyz.erupt:erupt; it is a mall demo entity in erupts/erupt-example whose image field is EditType.ATTACHMENT with AttachmentType.Type.IMAGE. At tag 1.12.19 the handler requires an Erupt session token plus GoodsCategory menu access and add/edit power, then ImageIO.read() rejects non-images before storage. Uploaded bytes are written under erupt.uploadPath (keepUploadFileName default false; random basename plus original extension) and served as Spring static resources at /erupt-attachment/**, which does not execute JSP/PHP/webshells. The supporting gist has no PoC. The claimed CWE-434 RCE is therefore not a security issue in this product.
flaw_origin: False positive advisory, not a code defect. MITRE CNA record remains PUBLISHED (not REJECTED/WITHDRAWN); GitHub GHSA withdrawn_at is null; NVD status is Analyzed. The CafeD1 gist is a four-line template asserting 'any file upload' and webshell site takeover with no request, payload, or bypass. The named component is a Type.IMAGE demo field that has been ImageIO-gated since at least erupt 1.6.12, and git diff 1.12.19..1.12.20 on the upload controller/service/annotation is empty, matching GHSA first_patched_version=null. CISA-ADP CVSS 3.1 AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:R/S:U/C:L/I:L/A:N also contradicts RCE. No BIC or fix is assigned because the advisory itself is wrong.

reasoning: Vulnerability-first: the published claim is that erupt v1.12.19 /upload/GoodsCategory/image accepts a crafted file and yields arbitrary code execution (gist: any-file upload including webshells). First-party records were checked before history search. CVE.org state is PUBLISHED (not rejected/withdrawn); NVD is Analyzed; GHSA withdrawn_at is null, so this is not a withdrawn-advisory close. The only technical reference is the CafeD1 gist, which contains no reproduction. The path matches EruptFileController.upload, i.e. POST /erupt-api/file/upload/{erupt}/{field}. GoodsCategory does not exist in the assigned erupt clone; it lives in erupts/erupt-example as a 2021 mall demo whose image field is AttachmentType.Type.IMAGE. At the cited tag 1.12.19 that field therefore hits the IMAGE branch, which always calls ImageIO.read and rejects a non-image (plain JSP/PHP/webshell). The endpoint is also behind EruptRouter ERUPT verification (session token + menu) and powerLegal add/edit, so it is not unauthenticated. Successful IMAGE uploads are stored under the configured upload directory and served with Spring's static resource handler at /erupt-attachment/**; that stack does not compile or execute uploaded JSP/PHP. keepUploadFileName defaults false, so the stored name is a random 12-letter stem plus the client extension; even a polyglot image with a dangerous extension would be a static blob, not RCE. git diff 1.12.19..1.12.20 on the upload implementation is empty, and GHSA records no patched version, which is the expected vendor disposition when there is nothing to patch. CISA-ADP CVSS (UI:R, C:L, I:L, A:N) is internally inconsistent with the RCE narrative. Residual observations (IMAGE does not default-whitelist jpg/png; keepUploadFileName plus unsanitized '../' was later hardened) are not the advisory's mechanism and do not make the webshell-RCE claim true. Therefore the advisory itself is a false positive / not a security issue as stated. FALSE_POSITIVE does not require a BIC or fix SHA; AI authorship was not judged on any commit object.
